Ferdowsi.fact: However, he regards stories of travel to Baghdad and Isfahan—found in some manuscript prefaces and later accretions to the Shahnameh—as legendary.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: _____–1165; 560 AH)—the earliest author to write a dedicated account of Ferdowsi’s life—also located his birth in the village of “Bāz” (identified with Pazh)
Ferdowsi.fact: 1164–1165; 560 AH)—the earliest author to write a dedicated account of Ferdowsi’s life—also located his birth in the village of “Bāz” (identified with Pazh).

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Some later sources proposed nearby villages such as _____ and Razan, but many contemporary scholars consider these suggestions unsubstantiated
Ferdowsi.fact: Some later sources proposed nearby villages such as Shadab and Razan, but many contemporary scholars consider these suggestions unsubstantiated.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: A third time, at the close of the Shahnameh, he states that he was seventy-one and gives the completion date as _____–1010 (400 AH); subtracting seventy-one again points to 940
Ferdowsi.fact: A third time, at the close of the Shahnameh, he states that he was seventy-one and gives the completion date as 1009–1010 (400 AH); subtracting seventy-one again points to 940.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Rokn al-_____ proposed 925–926 (313 AH)
Ferdowsi.fact: Rokn al-Din Homayounfarrokh proposed 925–926 (313 AH).

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In various sources and in the prefaces of some _____ manuscripts, his name is reported as Mansur, Hasan, or Ahmad; his father’s as Hasan, Ahmad, or Ali; and his grandfather’s as Sharafshah
Ferdowsi.fact: In various sources and in the prefaces of some Shahnameh manuscripts, his name is reported as Mansur, Hasan, or Ahmad; his father’s as Hasan, Ahmad, or Ali; and his grandfather’s as Sharafshah. According to legend, Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni promised Ferdowsi a gold piece for every couplet of the Shahnameh, to be paid upon its completion.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Older sources such as ʿAjāʾib al-Makhlūqāt, _____’s Tarikh-e Gozideh, and an early “third” preface to the Shahnameh give his personal name as Hasan
Ferdowsi.fact: Older sources such as ʿAjāʾib al-Makhlūqāt, Hamdallah Mustawfi’s Tarikh-e Gozideh, and an early “third” preface to the Shahnameh give his personal name as Hasan.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Other sources—such as the _____ translation associated with al-Bundari of Isfahan, the “Florence manuscript” preface, and the Baysunghuri Preface and texts derived from it—report Mansur
Ferdowsi.fact: Other sources—such as the Arabic translation associated with al-Bundari of Isfahan, the “Florence manuscript” preface, and the Baysunghuri Preface and texts derived from it—report Mansur.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: For his father, Tarikh-e _____ and the same early preface give the name Ali
Ferdowsi.fact: Older sources such as ʿAjāʾib al-Makhlūqāt, Hamdallah Mustawfi’s Tarikh-e Gozideh, and an early “third” preface to the Shahnameh give his personal name as Hasan. For his father, Tarikh-e Gozideh and the same early preface give the name Ali.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Their children were raised with _____ etiquette and cultural norms and were seen as guardians of a national cultural memory
Ferdowsi.fact: Dehqāns were landholding elites in the early Islamic centuries who often converted to Islam in part to preserve their social and economic position, while maintaining a strong attachment to pre-Islamic Iranian customs and striving to protect inherited traditions. Their children were raised with Iranian etiquette and cultural norms and were seen as guardians of a national cultural memory.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In any case, the _____ provides no clear proof of Pahlavi literacy
Ferdowsi.fact: In any case, the Shahnameh provides no clear proof of Pahlavi literacy. The Shahnameh does contain occasional allusions to astronomy, philosophy, and other fields, but these do not by themselves demonstrate specialized mastery; what is unmistakable is Ferdowsi’s command of Persian language and of Iranian cultural-historical tradition.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Ferdowsi’s son is said to have died in _____–1006 (396 AH) at the age of thirty-seven, when Ferdowsi was sixty-seven; Ferdowsi laments this reversal of the natural order and prays for his son’s forgiv
Ferdowsi.fact: Ferdowsi’s son is said to have died in 1005–1006 (396 AH) at the age of thirty-seven, when Ferdowsi was sixty-seven; Ferdowsi laments this reversal of the natural order and prays for his son’s forgiveness.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: A narrative poem, Yūsof o _____ā (Joseph and Zuleika), was once attributed to him, but scholarly consensus now rejects the idea it is his
Ferdowsi.fact: A narrative poem, Yūsof o Zolaykā (Joseph and Zuleika), was once attributed to him, but scholarly consensus now rejects the idea it is his.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Introductions to some manuscripts of the _____ include verses purporting to be the satire
Ferdowsi.fact: Introductions to some manuscripts of the Shahnameh include verses purporting to be the satire. The beginning of Ferdowsi’s composition of the Shahnameh, based on the Shahnameh of Abu Mansur, is usually placed at around the age of thirty; however, judging from Ferdowsi’s poetic ability, it can be inferred that he also composed poetry in his youth, and may even have begun versifying parts of the Shahnameh at that time, drawing on older tales preserved in oral tradition among the people.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Modern scholarship has rejected this attribution; among others, Mojtaba Minovi concluded in _____ that its author was “a mediocre versifier named Shamsi”
Ferdowsi.fact: Modern scholarship has rejected this attribution; among others, Mojtaba Minovi concluded in 1976 that its author was “a mediocre versifier named Shamsi”.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In particular, the qasidas are often regarded as products of the _____ period
Ferdowsi.fact: In particular, the qasidas are often regarded as products of the Safavid period.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Later, around 980–981 CE, in the reign of _____ (Mansur’s son), and after the death of Daqiqi, he began versifying the prose Shahnameh of Abu Mansur
Ferdowsi.fact: Later, around 980–981 CE, in the reign of Nuh II (Mansur’s son), and after the death of Daqiqi, he began versifying the prose Shahnameh of Abu Mansur.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: It is thought that _____ had begun the versification of the Shahnameh by order of the Samanid ruler
Ferdowsi.fact: Later, around 980–981 CE, in the reign of Nuh II (Mansur’s son), and after the death of Daqiqi, he began versifying the prose Shahnameh of Abu Mansur. It is thought that Daqiqi had begun the versification of the Shahnameh by order of the Samanid ruler.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: However, after a friend from his hometown—identified in the _____ as Muhammad Lashkari—made a manuscript of that source available to him, he abandoned the journey and began the work in his own city
Ferdowsi.fact: However, after a friend from his hometown—identified in the Baysonghori Preface as Muhammad Lashkari—made a manuscript of that source available to him, he abandoned the journey and began the work in his own city.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: At first he benefited from the patronage of Amirak Mansur, son of _____ ibn ‘Abd al-Razzaq, but this period did not last long and ended with Mansur’s death
Ferdowsi.fact: Accordingly, Ferdowsi initially intended to travel to Bukhara—the Samanid capital—to obtain authorization to continue Daqiqi’s work, secure financial support, and consult a copy of the prose Shahnameh compiled for Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Razzaq, which was presumably kept in the Samanid court library and used by Daqiqi. At first he benefited from the patronage of Amirak Mansur, son of Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Razzaq, but this period did not last long and ended with Mansur’s death.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Amirak Mansur was arrested in _____ around 987–988 CE, taken to Bukhara, and then killed
Ferdowsi.fact: Amirak Mansur was arrested in Nishapur around 987–988 CE, taken to Bukhara, and then killed.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: This was the first recension of the _____, and for nearly sixteen further years he worked to expand and refine it
Ferdowsi.fact: Ferdowsi completed the Shahnameh in about 994–995 CE, three years before Mahmud’s accession. This was the first recension of the Shahnameh, and for nearly sixteen further years he worked to expand and refine it.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: These years coincided with the fall of the Samanids and the rise of _____ of Ghazni
Ferdowsi.fact: These years coincided with the fall of the Samanids and the rise of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni. In about 1003–1004 CE, at the age of sixty-five, Ferdowsi decided to present the Shahnameh to Sultan Mahmud and therefore undertook a new recension.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In about _____–1004 CE, at the age of sixty-five, Ferdowsi decided to present the Shahnameh to Sultan Mahmud and therefore undertook a new recension
Ferdowsi.fact: In about 1003–1004 CE, at the age of sixty-five, Ferdowsi decided to present the Shahnameh to Sultan Mahmud and therefore undertook a new recension.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In the second recension he completed the portions relating to the reign of the _____ kings
Ferdowsi.fact: In the second recension he completed the portions relating to the reign of the Sasanian kings.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: The completion of the second recension is dated to 8 March _____, when Ferdowsi was seventy-one years old
Ferdowsi.fact: The completion of the second recension is dated to 8 March 1010, when Ferdowsi was seventy-one years old.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: May the body of _____ be ever prosperous; may his head be green, and his heart and soul rejoicing
Ferdowsi.fact: May the body of King Mahmud be ever prosperous; may his head be green, and his heart and soul rejoicing.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Now the tale of _____ is ended, in Spandarmad, on the day of Ard; From the Hijra, five times eighty have passed, in the name of the world-judging Creator
Ferdowsi.fact: Now the tale of Yazdegerd is ended, in Spandarmad, on the day of Ard; From the Hijra, five times eighty have passed, in the name of the world-judging Creator.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: There, with the assistance of the vizier Ahmad ibn _____, it was presented to the sultan
Ferdowsi.fact: There, with the assistance of the vizier Ahmad ibn Hasan Maymandi, it was presented to the sultan.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Based on remarks attributed to _____ and Farid al-Din Attar, the total time spent composing the Shahnameh is given as twenty-five years
Ferdowsi.fact: Based on remarks attributed to Nizami Aruzi and Farid al-Din Attar, the total time spent composing the Shahnameh is given as twenty-five years.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In the _____-nama, however, “thirty years” is mentioned in three places, and “thirty-five years” once
Ferdowsi.fact: On the basis of a verse in the Hajw-nama, Ferdowsi again refers to his age in the years after the completion of the Shahnameh, calling himself eighty years old: Now my life has neared eighty; my hope has all at once been blown away. In the Hajw-nama, however, “thirty years” is mentioned in three places, and “thirty-five years” once.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: If one assumes a start date of 978–979 and an end date of _____, the period of composition would amount to thirty-three years
Ferdowsi.fact: If one assumes a start date of 978–979 and an end date of 1010, the period of composition would amount to thirty-three years. According to Jalal Khaleghi-Motlagh, considering the date of composition of “Bijan and Manijeh” and Ferdowsi’s revisions after 1010, Ferdowsi devoted about thirty-five years of his life to the Shahnameh.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: According to Jalal Khaleghi-Motlagh, considering the date of composition of “Bijan and Manijeh” and Ferdowsi’s revisions after _____, Ferdowsi devoted about thirty-five years of his life to the Shahna
Ferdowsi.fact: If one assumes a start date of 978–979 and an end date of 1010, the period of composition would amount to thirty-three years. According to Jalal Khaleghi-Motlagh, considering the date of composition of “Bijan and Manijeh” and Ferdowsi’s revisions after 1010, Ferdowsi devoted about thirty-five years of his life to the Shahnameh.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Scholars such as Nöldeke, _____, and Safa have likewise maintained that the Hajw-nama has an authentic core and that some of its verses may be genuine
Ferdowsi.fact: Scholars such as Nöldeke, Taqizadeh, and Safa have likewise maintained that the Hajw-nama has an authentic core and that some of its verses may be genuine.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Based on the verse in the Hajw-nama that refers to Ferdowsi’s eightieth year, it is dated to before about _____
Ferdowsi.fact: Based on the verse in the Hajw-nama that refers to Ferdowsi’s eightieth year, it is dated to before about 1018.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: According to _____, the Saffarids—especially Ya'qub ibn al-Layth—played a prominent role in the expansion of Persian literature
Ferdowsi.fact: According to Morteza Ravandi, the Saffarids—especially Ya'qub ibn al-Layth—played a prominent role in the expansion of Persian literature.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: At that time, _____ and Arabic books were written in the capital and other cities, and the library of Bukhara amazed scholars such as Ibn Sīnā
Ferdowsi.fact: According to Morteza Ravandi, the Saffarids—especially Ya'qub ibn al-Layth—played a prominent role in the expansion of Persian literature. At that time, Persian and Arabic books were written in the capital and other cities, and the library of.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: According to Frye, this renaissance was an _____–Iranian “Renaissance” nurtured under the Samanids, whose Iranian aspect outweighed its Arabic aspect
Ferdowsi.fact: According to Frye, this renaissance was an Islamic–Iranian “Renaissance” nurtured under the Samanids, whose Iranian aspect outweighed its Arabic aspect.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: By this process, the _____ helped make Islam a world culture and showed that Islam need not be tied to the Arabic language
Ferdowsi.fact: According to Frye, this renaissance was an Islamic–Iranian “Renaissance” nurtured under the Samanids, whose Iranian aspect outweighed its Arabic aspect. By this process, the Samanids helped make Islam a world culture and showed that Islam need not be tied to the Arabic language.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In this period, religious and non-religious works were translated from Arabic into _____ (Dari)
Ferdowsi.fact: In this period, religious and non-religious works were translated from Arabic into Persian (Dari). Balʿamī translated the History of al-Ṭabarī from Arabic into Persian.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Balʿamī translated the _____ of al-Ṭabarī from Arabic into Persian
Ferdowsi.fact: Balʿamī translated the History of al-Ṭabarī from Arabic into Persian. Daqiqi began versifying Iran’s pre-Islamic history by order of Nuh II, but his death left the project unfinished—work that Ferdowsi later completed, thereby preserving, to some extent, the heritage of Middle Persian literature from being lost.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Works on medicine and pharmacology were written, and al-_____ compiled an encyclopedic work
Ferdowsi.fact: Works on medicine and pharmacology were written, and al-Khwarizmi compiled an encyclopedic work.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Ravandi says that, accordingly, many _____ scholars and writers took steps to revive the History of ancient Iran
Ferdowsi.fact: In Ferdowsi’s time, the intensity of the Shu'ubiyya movement had somewhat diminished; nevertheless, some patriotic Iranians still reflected on their ancestral past. Ravandi says that, accordingly, many Iranian scholars and writers took steps to revive the History of ancient Iran.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: To that end, historical, literary, and social writings that had survived the _____ conquest were gathered and prepared as source material for the composition of histories and Shāhnāmas
Ferdowsi.fact: To that end, historical, literary, and social writings that had survived the Arab conquest were gathered and prepared as source material for the composition of histories and Shāhnāmas.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Abū al-Muʾayyad Balkhī wrote a prose Shāhnāma, and Masʿūdī _____ī composed one in verse
Ferdowsi.fact: Abū al-Muʾayyad Balkhī wrote a prose Shāhnāma, and Masʿūdī Marvazī composed one in verse.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: It is thought that they supported the emergence and growth of a poetic tradition that combined features of formal Arabic poetry with _____ customs preserved in popular and semi-popular verse
Ferdowsi.fact: These Iranian rulers—especially the Samanid amirs—sought to promote a national and patriotic literature; however, this aim should not be taken as the sole or fundamental motive, since a deep-rooted, broad-based movement grounded in social conditions produced this demand. It is thought that they supported the emergence and growth of a poetic tradition that combined features of formal Arabic poetry with Iranian customs preserved in popular and semi-popular verse.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Also, in the east, knowledge and use of _____ were less widespread, and Arabic as a literary language lacked the strength to prevent the emergence of a new language
Ferdowsi.fact: Unlike regions such as Fars and Jibal—closer to Baghdad and more strongly shaped by Arabic culture—in eastern Iran the class of dehqāns still endured, largely intact, and Arabic culture had only a limited effect on their daily life. It is thought that they supported the emergence and growth of a poetic tradition that combined features of formal Arabic poetry with Iranian customs preserved in popular and semi-popular verse.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Zoroastrianism (_____) and Devyasna traditions were not deeply rooted in that region; instead, Iranian culture persisted through many oral narratives and poems in Dari
Ferdowsi.fact: Zoroastrianism (Mazdayasna) and Devyasna traditions were not deeply rooted in that region; instead, Iranian culture persisted through many oral narratives and poems in Dari.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Yet this semi-popular culture—standing against the _____-influenced culture of the elite—required more elevated works to stand alongside Arabic-oriented culture
Ferdowsi.fact: Also, in the east, knowledge and use of Arabic were less widespread, and Arabic as a literary language lacked the strength to prevent the emergence of a new language. Yet this semi-popular culture—standing against the Arabic-influenced culture of the elite—required more elevated works to stand alongside Arabic-oriented culture.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Islam’s influence on these themes was limited, while their _____ roots were ancient and deep
Ferdowsi.fact: In Persian literature, epic poetry held a place alongside lyric poetry; epic as a genre was unfamiliar in Arabic poetry and was thoroughly Iranian, signaling the continuity of literature before and after Islam. Islam’s influence on these themes was limited, while their Iranian roots were ancient and deep.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Even some lyrical themes, such as descriptions of nature, had roots in pre-_____ literature
Ferdowsi.fact: Even some lyrical themes, such as descriptions of nature, had roots in pre-Islamic literature.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In the _____ myth, Ohrmazd is attacked by his counterpart Ahriman; similarly, the Shahnameh frequently portrays the div as a primordial enemy
Ferdowsi.fact: In the Zurvanite myth, Ohrmazd is attacked by his counterpart Ahriman; similarly, the Shahnameh frequently portrays the div as a primordial enemy. As an example, he interprets Zal’s white hair and Sam’s rejection of him not as a retelling of the Zurvanite account of Ahriman’s birth, but as reflecting a Mazdayasnian notion.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In the stories of _____, Siamak, Tahmuras, Hushang, and Jamshid, the div play a foundational role in shaping the narrative world
Ferdowsi.fact: In the stories of Keyumars, Siamak, Tahmuras, Hushang, and Jamshid, the div play a foundational role in shaping the narrative world.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Aydinlou also disputes the view that the religion of the _____’s kings prior to Goshtasp should be understood primarily as Zurvanite
Ferdowsi.fact: Other scholars have pointed to additional Mazdayasnian features in the Shahnameh, including references to the Zend and Avesta in stories set before the appearance of Zoroaster, the “three goods” associated with Mazdayasnian ethics, accounts of social groupings, praise of fire, and a number of idioms and motifs related to animals (including horses). Aydinlou also disputes the view that the religion of the Shahnameh’s kings prior to Goshtasp should be understood primarily as Zurvanite.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: On this view, the _____’s opening praise of God as “the Lord of life and wisdom” aligns with conceptions in which Ahura Mazda is associated with the originating substance of soul and intellect
Ferdowsi.fact: On this view, the Shahnameh’s opening praise of God as “the Lord of life and wisdom” aligns with conceptions in which Ahura Mazda is associated with the originating substance of soul and intellect. Elyas Nooraei similarly emphasizes light as a central theme in Khosravani wisdom and argues that it appears both in the Shahnameh and in Suhrawardi’s Illuminationism.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Qaemi adds that, based on current knowledge, it remains difficult to determine whether such formulations should be traced first to Greek thought or to traditions shaped by _____
Ferdowsi.fact: Qaemi adds that, based on current knowledge, it remains difficult to determine whether such formulations should be traced first to Greek thought or to traditions shaped by Zoroastrianism.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Elyas Nooraei similarly emphasizes light as a central theme in _____ wisdom and argues that it appears both in the Shahnameh and in Suhrawardi’s Illuminationism
Ferdowsi.fact: Farzad Qaemi describes the epistemic structure of Khosravani wisdom as grounded in the “emanation” of multiplicity from unity, such that each material entity is understood to have a supra-material archetype. Elyas Nooraei similarly emphasizes light as a central theme in Khosravani wisdom and argues that it appears both in the Shahnameh and in Suhrawardi’s Illuminationism.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: With the rise of _____, these materials were reworked, and under the Samanids a number of prose and verse “Shahnamehs” were produced
Ferdowsi.fact: With the rise of New Persian, these materials were reworked, and under the Samanids a number of prose and verse “Shahnamehs” were produced.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Similar assessments are associated with scholars such as Khaleghi-Motlagh, _____, and Dabirsiaghi
Ferdowsi.fact: Similar assessments are associated with scholars such as Khaleghi-Motlagh, Shapur Shahbazi, and Dabirsiaghi.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: It promoted the equal standing of peoples and criticized ethnic chauvinism as inconsistent with _____ teachings
Ferdowsi.fact: It promoted the equal standing of peoples and criticized ethnic chauvinism as inconsistent with Islamic teachings.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Over time, some writers associated with the trend produced polemics that emphasized the merits of non-_____ (ʿajam) and minimized Arab cultural contributions
Ferdowsi.fact: Over time, some writers associated with the trend produced polemics that emphasized the merits of non-Arabs (ʿajam) and minimized Arab cultural contributions.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: He also notes that a range of _____ groups shared with Shu‘ubiyya the principle of equality among Muslim peoples, and that a number of Shu‘ubiyya works are listed in Al-Fihrist
Ferdowsi.fact: He also notes that a range of Muslim groups shared with Shu‘ubiyya the principle of equality among Muslim peoples, and that a number of Shu‘ubiyya works are listed in Al-Fihrist.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: At the same time, lyric poetry developed through figures such as Rudaki and _____, while panegyric, didactic verse, and storytelling also became widespread
Ferdowsi.fact: At the same time, lyric poetry developed through figures such as Rudaki and Shahid Balkhi, while panegyric, didactic verse, and storytelling also became widespread.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In this view, without that prior maturation of _____, the Shahnameh would not have been possible
Ferdowsi.fact: In this view, without that prior maturation of New Persian, the Shahnameh would not have been possible.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Later scholarship has described _____, on the basis of the surviving corpus, as a capable poet whose contemporaries praised his talent
Ferdowsi.fact: Regarding Daqiqi, it has been argued that Ferdowsi’s decision to incorporate Daqiqi’s verses into the Shahnameh was motivated less by convenience than by a desire to preserve Daqiqi’s work. Ferdowsi frames this decision in the story of dreaming of Daqiqi, where Daqiqi requests that Ferdowsi not be “stingy” and include his verses.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: One example is _____āh-nāma by Fatḥ-‘Alī Ṣabā, composed in imitation of the Shahnameh and devoted to the military campaigns of Fatḥ-‘Alī Shāh
Ferdowsi.fact: One example is Shahanshāh-nāma by Fatḥ-‘Alī Ṣabā, composed in imitation of the Shahnameh and devoted to the military campaigns of Fatḥ-‘Alī Shāh.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Many plays have also been written on the basis of _____ narratives
Ferdowsi.fact: During the Bazgasht-e Adabī (“Literary Return”), alongside a renewed interest in poets such as Sa‘dī and Hāfeẓ and in poets such as ‘Onṣorī, Farrokhī, and Manūčehrī, Ferdowsi and his Shahnameh also received considerable attention. One example is Shahanshāh-nāma by Fatḥ-‘Alī Ṣabā, composed in imitation of the Shahnameh and devoted to the military campaigns of Fatḥ-‘Alī Shāh.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: His works are cited as a crucial component in the persistence of the _____ language, as those works allowed much of the tongue to remain codified and intact
Ferdowsi.fact: Ferdowsi is one of the undisputed giants of Persian literature. After Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, a number of other works similar in nature surfaced over the centuries within the cultural sphere of the Persian language.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Many modern _____ see him as the father of the modern Persian language
Ferdowsi.fact: Many modern Iranians see him as the father of the modern Persian language.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: In _____, Reza Shah set up a ceremony in Mashhad, Khorasan, celebrating a thousand years of Persian literature since the time of Ferdowsi, titled "Ferdowsi Millennial Celebration", inviting notable Eu
Ferdowsi.fact: In 1934, Reza Shah set up a ceremony in Mashhad, Khorasan, celebrating a thousand years of Persian literature since the time of Ferdowsi, titled "Ferdowsi Millennial Celebration", inviting notable European as well as Iranian scholars.

Ferdowsi.subject: Applied Sciences
Ferdowsi.question: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is a university established in _____ that also takes its name from Ferdowsi
Ferdowsi.fact: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is a university set up in 1949 that also takes its name from Ferdowsi.

Francine Descartes.fact: Helena may have moved with Descartes to his next addresses — including in 1643 to Egmond-Binnen — where in 1644 she married the local innkeeper Jan Jansz van Wel. Descartes himself would remain in Egmond-Binnen until 1649, the longest period he ever stayed at any residence.
